clauses.reason: The sole operative sentence says “I hereby revoke the said Executive Orders” Nos. 9698, 9751 and 9823 so far as they pertain, respectively, to the three named organizations. The order states no effective date, so the partial revocation took effect when signed on October 10, 1949; the filing stamp reads October 11, 1949, disclosed as the alternative if effectiveness is tied to filing. The command was exhausted by performance and the end source is the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10083 (14 FR 6161 (Federal Register of October 12, 1949)) was signed October 10, 1949. The filing stamp printed after the order reads October 11, 1949, one day after signing. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence beginning “NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 1 of the said International Organizations Immunities Act, I hereby revoke the said Executive Orders” and revoking those three orders only so far as they pertain to the three named organizations. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on October 10, 1949. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. No other held text cites this order's number by an order citation. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Orders Nos. 9698, 9751 and 9823, but only so far as they designated the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration, the Inter-American Coffee Board and the Intergovernmental Committee on Refugees as public international organizations remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.

savings.reason: The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Orders Nos. 9698, 9751 and 9823, but only so far as they designated the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration, the Inter-American Coffee Board and the Intergovernmental Committee on Refugees as public international organizations stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked. Executive Orders 9698, 9751 and 9823 remain in force as to the other organizations they designate; they are independent instruments and are not claimed here.
